issues.text: Design 4.9.1 lists the closed labels of mac() as session, csrfh, csrf, reauth, reset, recovery, ip, rl, delay, while 4.9.5 keys login_failures by mac("acct", email_norm). keys.js adds "acct" to MAC_LABELS (it is the label 4.9.5 names); no other label exists. CODE-DESIGNER may want 4.9.1 updated.

Design 5.3 says «auth_err_<code> for each of the 21 AUTH_CODES»; 4.8 and B7b give 23 (body_too_large and site_closed included). errors.js exports the 23 of 4.8; FRONTEND-DEV's texts.js needs a key for each of the 23 (TX-11).

Body shapes (4.4 gives the ranges, 4.1 the bad_body rule): login password and the current password ≤ 128 code points (more → bad_body); a new password (setup password, password next, reset password) is a text ≤ 1024 code points in the schema and its 10-128 rule is rules() → password_rules, as rows 4, 8, 10 require; setup token text ≤ 128 whose form is checked by the handler (→ the uniform 404, counted); reset code text ≤ 64 whose form is checked by the handler (→ reset_invalid, counted); purpose text ≤ 32 (→ unknown_purpose); code fields by their form (6 digits or 16 base32, a wrong form → bad_body). A route row has exactly method, path, meta, handler; its body shape is kept beside the row in a WeakMap of http/schema.js (withBody / bodyShapeOf); a planted row without a shape takes the empty body {}.

AuthDeps of 4.7 gains one optional key, txDeadlineMs (default TX_DEADLINE_MS 4000): the injection point that ADD-2 needs («deadline injected small»), probed with 300 and 600 ms. The request deadline is the request's start on performance.now() plus that value.

The audit writer's signature is appendAudit(q, entry, { now, mac }): the writer needs the clock time for created_at and the HMAC of keys.js for ip_hmac; entry keeps the fields of 4.11 (ip is the normalised address, stored only as mac("ip", ip)). verifyAudit(q) → { ok, count, badId? }; the admin route answers bad_id. readAuditPage orders by audit_log.id (an order by the aliased text id would sort 1, 10, 11 — caught by probe p2 and fixed before the hand-over).

Setup names the owner organisation with the admin's display name (4.4 row 4 gives no organisation name; orgs.name 1-120 holds the 1-80 name). The setup audit row: actor admin, target the new user, details {}. Failed logins: actor_kind system, target the account id or null, details.reason unknown_email, disabled (also for deleted), wrong_password, locked, delay, totp_missing, totp_wrong.

docs/security-invariants.md has the 13 rows of 4.14 with one test file and one test name each (SI-1 reads one file and one name per row): IS-1, RLS-1, IS-4, SC-7, CS-1, SS-1, LO-1, AC-2, SQL-1, LG-2, RT-3, DBC-1, RLS-5. The further names 4.14 mentions (IS-3, IS-5, LO-3, AUTH-RACE-1, RLS-4) are not rows of their own.

Seeds (6.2): the 0002 seed also holds `select setval('audit_log_id_seq', 2)` so that a writer on the seeded database continues the chain after the two seeded rows; every created_at/updated_at of a seeded row is a fixed literal (0001: platform_settings.updated_at), because the default now() made two databases «seeded alike» differ in content (probe p4 before the fix: platform_settings: differs: content).

The rehearsal job: seeds go to psql through `docker exec -i sai-reh psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d <db> -f - < <seed>`; step 14 is one `psql -c` of a constant do block with dollar-quoted strings; the dump file stays inside the container and is removed by the last step; the docker job's migration row is `test "$(… -Atc 'select name from schema_migrations order by name')" = "$(ls app/db/migrations | sort)"` (A13: the test's expected line follows this one). TEST-DESIGNER writes REHEARSAL_STEPS from the 18 step names of the job.

Step 11 of 4.7 updates auth_sessions.last_seen_at also on a returned refusal of a signed-in caller (a wrong current password, a wrong TOTP code): the «session rows unchanged» of SS-8 (and the like) hold for every column but last_seen_at, as CS-4 states for GET. A thrown refusal changes nothing (rollback).

pg.js does not await the ROLLBACK after a throw (a silent connection would otherwise delay the 503 past 4.9 s); the connection is released with release(true) when the ROLLBACK settles, and dropping it rolls back too. If the platform admin becomes inactive between the two reads of a login, the attempt takes the no-account branch (a second counter row after the delay row, only in that race).
